newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia anthrax outbreak spreads slightly.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia anthrax outbreak spreads slightly.

text.p: The outbreak of anthrax disease in cattle in the Australian state of Victoria had spread beyond the previous quarantine zone, a spokeswoman for the Department of Natural Resources and Environment (DNRE) said on Monday.
The number of cattle deaths also had risen, to 105, while 52 properties had now been confirmed to have anthrax, she said.
These figures are up from 77 deaths and 37 properties infected at Thursday of last week.
The spokeswoman told Reuters the anthrax outbreak appeared to be the biggest ever in Victoria.
But this state traditionally did not have a major problem with anthrax, with weather conditions usually more conducive to the disease in New South Wales and Queensland, she said.
The spread of the disease beyond the previous quarantine zone was to only a single property, about five km southeast of the previous confirmed area, she said.
More than 21,000 cattle had now been vaccinated, up from 11,000 last Thursday, and the vaccination campaign was continuing, she said.

The Department of Natural Resources and Environment said in a statement that staff were continuing to work around the clock in response to the anthrax outbreak, with the first outbreak reported on January 26, it said.
The department's pathology laboratory at Stanhope, in the infected area, had analysed 184 samples from animals with 119 proving negative to antrax, acting DNRE regional manager Chris McRae said.
Samples from any suspicious animal death in the area were sent to the laboratory, which had even tested a rat, two pigs and a horse, all of which tested negative to antrax, he said.
Extra vaccinations on properties surrounding anthrax-infected zones had been carried out to create a buffer zone of vaccinated properties, he said.
Investigations into the source of the outbreak were continuing but so far there were no leads, he said.
Australian officials have repeatedly stated that anthrax poses no threat to consumers of dairy produicts because of processing and other safeguards.
Australia exports about A$1.8 billion worth of processed dairy products a year, to Europe, the Middle East and Asia.
Japan, seen as the most sensitive market for exported Australian dairy products, so far has shown no major concern over the outbreak of the disease in Victoria.
The anthrax outbreak is in the Goulburn Valley area of Victoria between Tatura and Stanhope. The area supplies about 30 percent of Australia's dairy products.

Anthrax is a bacterial infection which causes rapid death in cattle, sheep and goats when they eat contaminated soil or feed and is propagated by hot, humid weather, especially after rain. It rarely affects humans although one meat industry worker has been infected during the latest outbreak, probably through a cut or scratch.
